paragraphs: Cities tend to be warmer than the countryside around them, and planners have long proposed painting roofs white as a remedy. A pale surface returns more sunlight to the sky, so a roof that once absorbed most of the incoming energy now absorbs considerably less, and the air above it stays cooler on summer afternoons. The strategy is not without cost, however. In winter, when the sun is low and heating is needed, the same reflective surface forgoes warmth that a dark roof would have captured, and in cold climates this can raise heating bills enough to cancel the summer savings. Modelers also note that the cooling effect at street level is modest, because most pedestrians stand well below the roofline. The measure therefore pays off chiefly in hot regions where air conditioning dominates energy use.
